From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: TraceBridge auth & rate-plan review for AtlasEdge on-prem visibility

Hi team — looping you in for a quick technical review. AtlasEdge's security team confirmed they will host the forwarder sidecar (TraceBridge) inside their VPC and forward logs/traces to our collector gateway. They asked for concrete auth and rate-limiting controls before the on-prem POC.

Key asks from AtlasEdge:
- Mutual TLS for the connection from TraceBridge -> Redwood collector (they prefer client certs).
- Per-tenant ingestion rate-limits with burst protection (to avoid noisy neighbors).
- Clear token rotation and evidence for key lifecycle (SOC2/Infosec audit).

Attached: tracebridge-auth-diagram.pdf (auth paths + cert flow) and siem-mapping-sample.log (sample event map).

Goals for this thread:
1) Confirm recommended auth modes we can support for on-prem (mTLS BYO-CA vs Redwood-managed certs).
2) Decide on rate-limiting scheme (fixed TPS per customer vs adaptive shaping).
3) Agree a minimal evidence pack AtlasEdge needs for their procurement (e.g., key rotation policy, acceptance tests).

Kimberly — can you call out constraints on the collector side (HEC token vs cert) and any implementation caveats? Marissa/Tessa — can you weigh in on the rollout/canary plan? Sara — if you can confirm the cert model AtlasEdge prefers, that will help us finalize the approach.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: Re: TraceBridge auth & rate-plan review for AtlasEdge on-prem visibility

Jordan — thanks, quick notes after looking at the diagram and sample mapping.

Short answers:
- Collector supports both HEC token + TLS and mutual TLS. For Splunk HEC-style ingestion we can accept a bearer token over TLS, but for the TraceBridge -> Collector control plane we recommend mTLS for stronger client auth.
- We can do BYO-CA (AtlasEdge provides certs) or Redwood-managed cert issuance. BYO-CA means we will only accept client certs signed by the provided CA bundle; Redwood-managed reduces onboarding friction but needs cross-org procurement for private CA sharing.

Rate-limiting options (pros/cons):
- Fixed per-tenant rate limit (e.g., 2000 events/sec): simple, predictable billing and safety.
- Adaptive shaping (based on moving average + burst window): better SLAs for spiky workloads but more operational complexity.

My recommendation: start with a conservative fixed ingress limit for the POC (500 eps) and enable a canary adaptive mode for one AZ after acceptance testing. That reduces risk for AtlasEdge and lets us tune limits.

Attachment notes: the siem-mapping-sample.log looks fine but we need a small script that validates HEC field mapping before acceptance (I'll attach a validator in a follow-up). Also recommend we add an IP allowlist option on the collector to reduce attack surface.

On evidence: provide key rotation cadence (we usually do 90 days for client certs, 30 days for bearer tokens used by ephemeral components) and a short checklist showing test vectors we run for mTLS + HEC acceptance.

--

Thanks Jordan/Kimberly — AtlasEdge security preferences below and a couple of clarifying Qs from procurement.

AtlasEdge preferences:
- We prefer mTLS with BYO-CA; security team will manage the private CA and roll certs via our internal PKI.
- We require per-tenant rate-limits enforced at ingestion with rejection semantics (4xx) and a configurable soft-burst for short spikes.
- Evidence needed: proof of key rotation process, acceptance test steps (mTLS handshake logs), and a sample of the logs you will store for 30/90/365 day retention buckets.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood provide a simple cert-acceptance script so our PKI team can automate signing checks?
2) What auditing logs will you make available to us for handoff (forensics in case of dropped events)?

Procurement notes: timeline is tight — they want technical acceptance by next Friday to align with their security review. If we can supply an evidence bundle + short runbook they can sign off quickly.

Sara Mueller
AtlasEdge — Security Engineering

Thanks for the quick turn, everyone. Summary and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Decisions agreed: 
- Auth model: BYO-CA mTLS for TraceBridge -> Redwood collector. AtlasEdge will provide CA bundle and rotation schedule; Redwood will configure collector to accept that CA bundle and verify client cert CNs.
- Rate-limits: start POC with fixed per-tenant ingress limit = 500 eps with a configurable soft burst (+50% for up to 30s). After 2-week canary we will evaluate enabling adaptive shaping for production.
- Evidence pack: we will produce a minimal evidence bundle containing:
  * cert rotation cadence and policy (90 days recommended for client certs)
  * mTLS acceptance test script (server-side handshake logs)
  * sample HEC mapping + retention buckets (30/90/365)

Rollout / canary plan: 
- Day 0: AtlasEdge deploys TraceBridge in staging VPC pointed at our staging collector (mTLS BYO-CA).
- Day 1–3: Acceptance tests run by AtlasEdge with our validator script.
- Day 4–17: Canary in AtlasEdge staging with fixed ingress limits (500 eps). Internal telemetry tracked via the Redwood Console (we will provide a read-only project view).
- Post-Canary: Joint review and decision to increase limit or enable adaptive shaping.

Action items: 
- Kimberly: drop the cert-acceptance script and a short validator (kimberly.park@redwood.com) — due EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa/Tessa: prepare a 2-week canary dashboard template and a simple rollback playbook — assignable to Marissa.
- Jordan: assemble evidence bundle and upload initial draft to Drive (link in metadata).
- Sara/AtlasEdge: share CA bundle and any internal PKI constraints by EOD Thursday so we can pre-configure the collector.

Attachments: initial-evidence-checklist.xlsx (I'll populate and iterate).

If anyone objects or wants changes to the plan, flag now — procurement needs sign-off by next Friday.

Thanks all,
Jordan
